trace: The date commonly given for Veramoor's founding is 1204. However, this date is poorly established. Tracing the citations reveals a circular and ultimately unsourced chain: the visit-veramoor page (P3) cites a history blog (P2), which cites an encyclopedia entry (P1), which cites a genealogy forum post (P5). That forum post (P5) is the original source — and it is merely a 2009 message-board comment from a user who explicitly says, 'I think Veramoor was founded around 1204, but I don't have a source for that.' The 'quick history facts' page (P4) also traces back into this same loop (citing P3). So although the 1204 date appears in multiple places and is described as 'well established' and 'widely documented,' all of those claims rest on a single speculative, admittedly unsourced guess. There is no independent or primary evidence supporting 1204; the apparent corroboration is an illusion created by citation circularity.
flagged: The date commonly given is 1204, but it is poorly established. Tracing the citations reveals a circular sourcing chain rather than independent confirmation: the genealogy forum post [P5] is the original source, where user 'histbuff' (in 2009) merely guessed 'around 1204' and explicitly admitted having no source. The encyclopedia [P1] cites that post and flags the date as UNVERIFIED. The medieval-history blog [P2] cites the encyclopedia [P1], the tourism site [P3] cites the blog [P2], and quick-history-facts [P4] cites the tourism site [P3]. So every claim that the date is 'well established' or 'widely documented' ultimately rests on a single unsourced, self-described guess. There is no independent or primary evidence supporting 1204, so the founding year should be treated as unverified and unreliable.
